requirements.requirement: Commands run through sudo are recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A valid sudoers configuration sets the required dedicated logfile and enables four-digit years; the securely permissioned log file was created. However, it remained empty and no successful sudo invocation or resulting entry was observed, so command, user, and timestamp capture were not functionally demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The installed and syntactically validated sudoers configuration explicitly disables sudo syslog logging with !syslog. No post-change sudo event was generated and compared against the dedicated and general logs, so isolation was not behaviorally verified.

overall_summary: The intended persistent sudo configuration was installed securely and passed visudo validation, but neither required behavior was directly demonstrated. The mandatory restart protocol captured the original boot identity and restart acknowledgement, but not a different post-restart identity or recovered service, data, and system state. Because restart persistence was not part of the public contract, that incomplete protocol lowers confidence rather than adding a task requirement.
limitations: The dedicated log was empty when observed, and all attempted sudo invocations hung in netlink_dump, preventing an end-to-end logging test.
No generated sudo event was checked for absence from /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/syslog.

Restart evidence is incomplete: the pre-restart boot identity was 267e568a-ef2b-4189-9a7f-50a72b044473 and the reboot was acknowledged, but every post-restart probe received connection reset, including the fixed after-executor observation.
The fixed lifecycle cross-check confirms the same pre-restart boot identity before preparation, but provides no post-restart boot identity or recovered health state.
Post-executor service health, package health, listening sockets, temporary files, and retained configuration could not be observed because node1 was unreachable.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Writing the sudoers fragment and dedicated log was directly required (cmd-39e286989d584387), and the asynchronous reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-80dfd5c6526d4f2a). Earlier sudo probes became stuck but served to discover the pre-existing kernel-level blocker and show why functional testing was unsafe; there is no evidence of persistent configuration damage from them. Hygiene cannot be fully established because node1 never became observable after the reboot, so failed services, package health, temporary residue—including the bounded reboot log—and final accessibility could not be checked.
